question.leadin: Give the following about lunar exploration.
question.text: Every mission which put people on the moon was part of this NASA program; the 11th, 12th, and 14th through 17th missions of this name were successful at that goal
question.clue: Edward White, Roger Chaffee, and Gus Grissom died in a fire that derailed its first mission.

swap.text: Clinton's victory in the 1992 election has been linked to this third-party candidate, whose campaign drew voters away from Bush. This billionaire owner of Electronic Data Systems died in 2019.
swap.answerHtml: Ross Perot (accept Henry Ross Perot; accept Henry Ray Perot)
swap.clue: During this man's best-known political campaign, he ran half-hour long television commercials featuring him talking about his life and his policies.

question.text: During the term of this president, tensions were heightened when the Soviets shot down an American U2 spy plane. This former World War II general spearheaded the construction of the Interstate Highway system.
question.answerHtml: Dwight D. Eisenhower [or Dwight David Eisenhower or David Dwight Eisenhower or Ike Eisenhower]
question.clue: This politician stated that "it is humanity hanging from a cross of iron" during a speech that listed alternatives to building a heavy bomber.

swap.text: One of the largest riots in United States history occurred in New York in 1863 when this system was instituted, and it also was a motivation behind many student riots during the Vietnam War before this system was discontinued in 1973.
swap.clue: The Catonsville Nine was a group of Catholic agitators who burned documents related to this process in 1968.

question.leadin: While the US provided large amounts of monetary support to the South Vietnamese government, it did not provide overt military aid until 1964.
question.text: Name this "attack" on the USS Maddox that prompted Congress to issue the Southeast Asia Resolution that permitted President Lyndon Johnson to deploy conventional forces in Southeast Asia.
question.clue: This event, which shared its name with a French protectorate, began when the USS Maddox fired warning shots at torpedo boats commanded by Le Duy Khoai.

swap.text: Published in advance of the baby boom, this doctor's book on child-rearing, The Common Sense Book of Baby and Child Care, was the second-most-sold book of the 20th century in America.

question.leadin: This president's National Commission on Excellence in Education criticized the country's schools in the report A Nation at Risk.
question.text: Name this president whose other children-related policies included the anti-drug "Just Say No" campaign, which was devised by his wife.
question.clue: This president authorized the overthrow of Hudson Austin in Operation Urgent Fury, the invasion of Grenada.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about the summer of 1969 in U.S. history.
swap.text: Michael Collins manned the command module Columbia during this NASA mission, during which the Eagle lander brought the first humans to the moon's surface.
swap.clue: Jim Lovell was removed from it in favor of Michael Collins.

question.leadin: Following World War II, many executives of American firms went into government service.
question.text: One of the two executives named Charlie Wilson to serve in senior government roles in the 1940s is widely misquoted as having told Congress that "What's good for [this company] is good for the country."
question.clue: This company sued NBC after Dateline aired a deceptive report entitled "Waiting to Explode" about one of its products.

swap.leadin: This event was sparked by thousands of people who rushed the Peruvian embassy trying to seek asylum.
swap.text: Name this 1980 event in which large numbers of people, many of them released prisoners, boarded ramshackle crafts headed to Florida from the namesake town.
swap.answerHtml: Mariel Boatlift [prompt on but DO NOT REVEAL Cuban Boatlift]
swap.clue: Some participants in this event staged a riot at Fort Chaffee, Arkansas, which briefly derailed the career of Governor Bill Clinton.

question.leadin: Hugh Thompson, Jr. ordered his men to turn their weapons on other American soldiers during this event.
question.text: Name this 1968 event, during which forces under William Calley massacred hundreds of civilians in the namesake hamlet during the Vietnam war. This event took place in a location codenamed "Pinkville."
question.clue: A helicopter pilot named Hugh Thompson was awarded several medals for his role in this event, as Thompson had tried to stop Ernest Medina from participating in this incident.

swap.leadin: Name these twentieth-century U.S. Secretaries of State.
swap.text: This Truman appointee and target of McCarthy attacks wrote the autobiography Present at the Creation.
swap.clue: He was an early supporter of dismissing Douglas MacArthur from command of UN forces in Korea.

question.leadin: Answer the following about failed presidential assassinations.
question.text: This President survived two assassination attempts in 17 days, which were the only assassination attempts carried out by women. One of the assassins was a member of the Manson Family.
question.clue: Two assassination attempts were made on this president in Sacramento.

swap.leadin: Answer some things about America's true favorite pastime, drinking.
swap.text: Mafia boss Frank Costello claims that the patriarch of this family got his start bootlegging, though there's little hard evidence for this. One of his sons, John, was president during the Cuban Missile Crisis and another, Teddy, was often our drunkest Senator.
swap.clue: Another politician with this surname was killed at the Ambassador Hotel by Sirhan Sirhan during a 1968 presidential campaign.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about an electoral ass-whooping.
question.text: While serving as a Senator from Minnesota, this man opposed the Vietnam War as a member of the Church Committee. He campaigned for the Democratic presidential nomination by questioning Gary Hart using the Wendy's slogan "Where's the Beef?"

swap.text: After Tydings' defeat, most of the members of the Tydings Committee worked for a similar committee named for this Nevada Democrat, the namesake and sponsor of the 1950 Internal Security Act passed over Truman's veto.
swap.clue: This senator was an avid admirer of Francisco Franco and a strong opponent of communist expansion. In 2017, a movement surfaced to rename his namesake airport in Las Vegas after Harry Reid.

question.leadin: Identify the following about some participants in the Watergate scandal who later wrote books about it.
question.text: Jeb Stuart Magruder, the author of An American Life: One Man's Road to Watergate served as the deputy director of this organization. It had the appropriate acronym of "CREEP".
question.answer: The Committee to Reelect the President
question.clue: This organization caused the Watergate break-in to become a full-fledged scandal after they paid for the burglars' legal fees. This organization was created to help a certain man win the election of 1972.

swap.leadin: Identify these figures associated with the presidential election of 1972, FTSNOP.
swap.text: This South Dakota senator replaced vice-presidential candidate Thomas Eagleton with Sargent Shriver after winning the Democratic nomination.
swap.clue: This man's initial Vice Presidential running mate, Thomas Eagleton, was controversially dropped and replaced with Sargent Shriver; that gaffe cost this Democrat every state but Massachusetts.

question.text: A Congressman from Illinois throughout the 1960s and 1970s, this Rockefeller Republican said in a debate that he regretted voting for the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution. He then ran as an Independent, but despite the support of several prominent liberals and independents, he mustered just 6 million votes in the November election.
question.clue: After losing the Republican nomination, this man ran as an independent, campaigning for a gas tax hike. Support from Rockefeller Republicans and intellectuals netted him seven percent of the vote.

swap.leadin: A Berkeley Barb hoax fooled the author of this book into including instructions for using banana peels to make the psychoactive drug bananadine.
swap.text: Name this book that William Powell published as a teenager in 1971. It contains instructions for synthesizing LSD, lock picking, phone phreaking, and making Molotov cocktails.
